root.name: Blackmar-Diemer Gambit Accepted: Euwe Defense
root.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. e4 dxe4 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. f3 exf3 5. Nxf3 e6

overview: Black has taken the gambit pawn and builds a compact set-up with ...e6, keeping the c8 bishop free of the usual Ng5 and Bg5 tricks. White continues 6.Bd3 or 6.Bg5 Be7 7.Bd3 with quick development, castling and attacking ideas against h7, Ne5 and Qe2/Qd2. Black plays ...c5, ...Nc6, ...O-O and tries to catch up in development and give back the pawn at the right moment. Experts regard the Euwe as one of Black's safest answers, so White needs real attacking chances to compensate.

white_ideas.idea: Develop Bd3, Bg5, O-O and Qe2 to attack on the kingside and the h7 square
Use the f3 knight and e5/Ng5 jumps with tactics against h7
Keep the d4 centre and the open e- and f-files for rooks

black_ideas.idea: Hold the pawn with ...Be7, ...O-O, ...c5 and neutralise the bishops
Challenge d4 with ...c5 and ...Nc6 to gain activity
Exchange pieces and play for an endgame with the extra pawn

typical_structures.structure: White d4 against Black e6 with the d- and f-files open; Black is a pawn up and the position is open for the pieces

character.notes: White develops rapidly with threats against h7 and Black is a pawn up and short of space: forcing play. Sharp.

gambit.notes: Black is a pawn up and can hold it; White gets only development.

soundness.notes: Strong players regard the BDG as unsound against accurate play; the Euwe is a safe defence. Dubious for White.

structure.notes: Open lines and diagonals; the e-pawn is the only Black centre pawn. Open.

approach.notes: Strong players seldom play the BDG. Offbeat.

level.notes: A dubious gambit is never Beginner; Intermediate because the attack depends on tactics and traps.

plan_phrases: lead in development for a pawn

sublines_that_differ.name: Zilbermints Gambit
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. e4 dxe4 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. f3 exf3 5. Nxf3 e6 6. Bg5 Be7 7. Bd3 Nc6 8. O-O Nxd4 9. Kh1
sublines_that_differ.how: Black takes on d4 and White tries a quick attack with extra material given.

sublines_that_differ.name: Duthilleuk Gambit
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. e4 dxe4 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. f3 exf3 5. Nxf3 e6 6. Bd3 Nc6 7. Bg5 Be7 8. Ne4
sublines_that_differ.how: A further sacrifice for tempo and attack.

character.reason: White is a pawn down for rapid attack; both sides need exact play.

gambit.reason: White gave a pawn that Black has taken and can keep.

soundness.reason: The Euwe is a solid answer and White's compensation is judged insufficient.

structure.reason: Open lines for the pieces, with few pawns in the centre.

approach.reason: Seldom chosen by strong players; played for surprise and attack.

level.reason: A dubious gambit is never Beginner; relies on tactics and known traps.

plans.reason: White compensates for the pawn with development and attacking chances.
